messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert — 3 containers in us-west-2/gpu-pool restarted in last 12m. Symptoms: CUDA OOM followed by container crash and node flap. Telemetry shows growing resident set on paged-attn allocator and rising kvcache slab fragmentation. Possible slow leak/fracture. Tagging on-call.
alex: Oncall here. I'm looking at the node list and crash logs. Are we seeing a spike in long-context requests? :thinking_face:
mira: yes — increase in 32k+ context sessions to a subset of endpoints. Noted sustained prefix cache churn for those requests.
sam: attaching quick log excerpt and OOM trace
sam: ```
[2026-10-03T04:12:05Z] runtime: gpu0: CUDA OOM: alloc 1.2G
[2026-10-03T04:12:05Z] kv_allocator: slab_alloc failed, free=48MB, requested=1.2G
[2026-10-03T04:12:06Z] container: pid 2378 killed (OOM)
[2026-10-03T04:12:06Z] node: kubelet eviction threshold breached -> node cordon
```
alex: that slab_alloc failure + tiny free pool is classic micro-fragmentation of paged-kv. Evictions not reclaiming because many small pinned pages.
mira: trying a live mitigation: increase kvcache eviction aggressiveness for affected model routes and enable immediate slab compaction on runtime.
jia: how do we flip that without redeploy? Can we hit runtime admin API to force compaction and lower prefix cache TTL for those routes?
luis: yes — runtime admin supports /admin/kv/compact and /admin/cache/ttl. I'm running the commands now on the two affected hosts.
ops-bot: Running: curl -XPOST https://rt-admin.us-west-2.internal/admin/kv/compact?force=true --data '{"pools":["paged-attn","kv-cache"]}'
luis: compaction started, estimated 45s.
alex: also bumping evict_ratio on route group `large-context-prod` from 0.15 -> 0.4 to free more reclaimed space. Doing this via config rollout with zero-downtime.
mira: rolling restart of the specific worker containers might be needed if compaction doesn't free enough contiguous slabs. Planning one-by-one restart to avoid capacity hole.
sam: note — fallback plan is to route large-context traffic to a lower-memory quantized model variant to reduce KV pressure. Need approval to flip traffic to quant-v2.
alex: approved. Default fallback policy already exists but not enabled for these routes; enabling now. This will buy time while we defrag.
incident-bot: :white_check_mark: compaction completed on host gpu-12; reclaimed ~1.1GB contiguous memory, fragmentation reduced from 87% -> 22% (kv bitmap scan)
mira: good signal on gpu-12. gpu-13 compaction still running. Observed one crash on gpu-11 during peak — it flapped out of the pool earlier.
luis: kicked a one-by-one rolling restart on workers on gpu-11 and gpu-14 to clear stale allocations. Restarts are in progress.
alex: updated rate limiters for the `large-context-prod` route: soft limit 20r/s -> 12r/s to reduce churn. Monitoring.
sam: inflight metrics: token/sec for large-context down ~48%, nodes overall CPU stable, tail-latency unchanged for 95th.
mira: customer-impact check: top 3 tenants that hit large-context routes — org-a, org-b, org-c. org-a saw 502s for ~3 minutes, org-b had elevated latency, org-c unaffected due to region routing.
alex: pinging SE for org-a to pre-empt tickets. @mira can you draft a short blurb about mitigation and expected recovery window?
mira: on it. Draft: "We observed intermittent service restarts due to GPU memory fragmentation affecting large-context endpoints. We applied live compaction, increased eviction aggressiveness, and routed heavy requests to fallback model variants. Most traffic recovered within 10 minutes; full remediation requires a patch to allocator compaction heuristics."
jia: note for postmortem — need longer-term: (1) proactive slab defrag schedule during low-traffic windows, (2) improve bitmap scanning to detect micro-frags earlier, (3) auto-fallback enablement when fragmentation > 60%.
luis: I pushed a temporary hotfix to runtime to expose a metric kvcache_fragmentation_ratio and an alert at 65%. Will roll to prod after midnight.
ops-bot: Action items created: #INC-2109 (live mitigation), #ENG-5271 (allocator heuristics), #SRE-402 (compaction schedule). Assigned to luis, mira, alex respectively.
alex: handoff to next on-call in 45m. Current state: compaction completed on 3/4 hosts, rolling restarts ongoing, fallback routing enabled, customer impact mitigated for org-a with SRE-owned note sent. Monitoring shows fragmentation ratio trending down.
mira: adding final remediation notes to the thread and linking traces. Will keep watch until next handoff. If anything spikes, escalate to infra oncall.
sam: saving crash dumps to /var/backups/incidents/2001112223/ for postmortem.
luis: I'll follow up with a short runbook patch for this specific pattern: "paged-kv micro-fragmentation -> compaction -> soften eviction -> route fallback -> rolling restart".
alex: thanks team. Handoff: @mira will be primary for next 2h; @luis will take infra escalations. Tagging next-oncall: @sam for logs.
ops-bot: :white_check_mark: Handoff logged. Next oncall: mira. Estimated incident close window: 3h for full rollout of allocator fix, mitigated for customers now.
mira: closing note: if we still see repeated small OOMs after compaction, we should consider lowering max-context for affected routes until allocator fix lands.
alex: copy. I'll update the incident doc and add timeline + tenants impacted.
